summary.intent: Plan and execute phase 49 (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation unwrap consolidation), then run the full PR-QA pipeline (simplify, security-review, CodeRabbit CLI) before pushing and creating a PR, followed by resolving CodeRabbit's GitHub review post-PR.
summary.outcome: Planning completed (5 plans / 3 waves, 6 requirements, plan-check passed after one revision round). Execution completed waves 1–3 plans 49-01 through 49-04; plan 49-05 (e2e) was dispatched but the transcript ends before confirming its result. PR-QA steps (simplify, security-review, CodeRabbit, push, PR creation) had not yet run.

repo: `reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange` (reencrypt.ts:49) is fully key-agnostic — takes raw sourceFolderKey/destFolderKey/fileIpnsPrivateKey with no owner vs. recipient distinction; reusable verbatim for the shared-folder case.

`share_keys` entries are keyed by `itemId` (file UUID), not by parent folder path — download path resolves `k.keyType === 'file' && k.itemId === item.id`, so file keys do NOT need re-registration after a folder move.

`adoptSharedFolderResult` emits `sharedFolder:updated` with `live.ipnsName` (always the active/source depth); the projection filters by `shareId` only, so calling adopt for the destination would corrupt the rendered view — call it once for the source result only.
Collision policy in `sdkCore.moveItem` is throw ('An item with this name already exists in destination'), not auto-rename — propagates through `runWrite` → `p.setError`.
The `SharedFolderClient` Pick allowlist (shared-folder-projection.ts:28-38) only listed the 7 Phase 48 methods; `moveInSharedFolder` and `enumerateSharedSubtree` both needed to be added.

File IPNS key for re-encryption must come from `share_keys keyType:'file-ipns'`, not `FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` — the latter is owner-wrapped and recipients cannot decrypt it (same pattern as `updateSharedFileHandler`).

Batch move in the private vault loops single-item `client.moveItem` via `useFileBrowserActions` selection Set → `handleBatchMoveConfirm` → `useFolderMutations.handleMoveItems`; the private `MoveDialog` already supports an `items` prop.

Drag-and-drop move lives in `FileListItem` (handleDragStart is multi-select-aware → drop target on folder rows → `handleDropOnFolder` → `moveItem`/`moveItems`); the shared side had none of this before phase 49.
`useSharedWriteOps.test.ts` already exists — the REQ-3 fix was to extend it with a `moveItemHandler` case rather than create a new file.
The web package has no `typecheck` npm script; the correct gate is `tsc -b` run from the web package root.
Intel API surface regeneration (`gsd-tools regen-intel`) can return empty when the regex extractor is unpopulated — it is a HINT-only artifact and should be omitted from planner prompts when empty.

code.finding: `reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange` signature is key-agnostic (raw bytes, no owner/recipient coupling) — safe to call from shared-folder move handler without modification.
`sdkCore.moveItem` throws on name collision — no auto-rename; callers must surface the error via `p.setError`.
Pick allowlist for `SharedFolderClient` — must be kept in sync when new methods are added to the client; Phase 49 added `moveInSharedFolder` and `enumerateSharedSubtree` here.

workflow: Sequential plan execution (no worktrees) is more reliable for AFK/autonomous runs than parallel-worktree mode — the merge-back protocol is error-prone to hand-drive due to cwd-drift and merge-base footguns.

After adding new public methods to an SDK package, the SDK dist must be explicitly rebuilt (e.g., `pnpm --filter sdk build`) before downstream web packages can typecheck against them — `index.d.ts` is a barrel re-export; new methods land in `client.d.ts`.

The GSD plan-checker runs in iteration loops; iteration 1 caught a real gap (REQ-3 had no dedicated web unit test, causing its verify step to pass vacuously) that required a targeted planner revision before proceeding.
The AI-SPEC gate can false-positive on the keyword `eval` appearing in e2e requirement prose — treat as non-blocking when there is zero actual AI content in the phase.

Disabling commit signing locally (`git config --local commit.gpgsign false`) before an AFK autonomous run prevents the 1Password signer from wedging; re-enable with `git config --local --unset commit.gpgsign` and note that signed rebase or admin override will be needed before merge if the repo enforces signed commits on PRs.
CodeRabbit posts a GitHub review automatically after PR creation — the workflow is: CodeRabbit CLI review (pre-PR) → push → create PR → wait for CodeRabbit GitHub review → run `/resolve-pr-reviews`.
gsd-tools is not on PATH inside planner-revision subagents — any commits the revision subagent intends to make must be done by the orchestrator after the subagent returns.

friction: AI-SPEC gate false-positived on 'eval' in e2e requirement text, requiring manual override to proceed.
